rows.whyStopped: The family's one pinned source binds byte-exact and is held. It cannot back the component it is mapped to. The committed packet set for mt_deferred_dismissal-set has FIVE required components, and the fourth, `mt_deferred_dismissal-primary-filing-4`, is declared outputStrategy `official_pdf_fill` against officialFormId `EXPUNGEMENTREMOVALREQUESTFORM.DOCX` - a Microsoft Word document. There is no PDF representation of those pinned bytes in any custody mounted here, so there is no page to overlay and no widget to fill.
theThreeRecordsThatAgreeOnTheComponentSe: data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json - track mt_deferred_dismissal, packetSet.components: five components, component 4 outputStrategy official_pdf_fill / officialFormId EXPUNGEMENTREMOVALREQUESTFORM.DOCX, requirement "required"
data/record-clearing/legal-design-packet-set-manifests.json - packetSetId mt_deferred_dismissal-set: the identical five-component set

data/record-clearing/legal-design-specifications.json - officialFormAssignments carries component 4 with mappingStatus "not_mapped"; customPleadingSpecs carries components 1, 2 and 3 with templateStatus "not_drafted"
whyNotConvertedOrSubstituted: CONVERTING IS NOT BINDING. LibreOffice is present in this container, so a DOCX-to-PDF conversion was technically available and was not used. A converted page is not the official form's bytes: its layout is renderer- and font-dependent, no committed record attests it, and a source-receipt binding the DOCX digest to pages that are not those bytes is a misleading receipt, not a bound one. Overlay coordinates measured against a locally-rendered document are also not reproducible by the Captain or by an independent verifier.

THE 2023 PDF IS NOT THIS SOURCE. The Nationwide recovery pool does hold a PDF of this form - `LegalEase Montana/2023-Updated-ExpungementRemovalRequestForm.pdf`, sha256 0362b43d05284210ec0aa0ca1a43e250351456c73880ec1581fbb78f467c99ee - and it is the wrong edition. The committed track registry resolves the point expressly: "Master Library Edition 1.1 retains the 2024 version as the supporting-process asset and does not retain the 2023 PDF. The 2024 version is used for legal design and the 2023 version is preserved as history only." The two editions also differ on what the participant must enclose: the 2023 version requires photo identification and the "Original Court Order"; the 2024 version drops the photo-ID requirement, requires the "Original Court Judgement" instead, and adds "Deferred Prosecution" to the fourth request type. Building the participant's DOJ submission on the superseded edition would tell them to enclose the wrong documents, and CAPTAIN_SOURCE_IDENTITY_DETERMINATIONS.json states the governing rule directly: a determination "never satisfies one identity by binding the binary of another".

COMPOSING A REPLACEMENT IS INVENTING A DOJ FORM. The committed unit description for mt-deferred-criss-submission calls the CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form "the required and only vehicle for the DOJ stage of four Montana tracks". A composed page bearing the shape of a Department of Justice form is a fabricated agency instrument.
rows.whyNotBuiltWithoutThatComponent: Dropping component 4 and shipping the four composed pages would zero the counters and shrink the delivery. The committed record names that exact outcome as the Montana failure mode: "A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check." Section 46-18-204(2) puts the DOJ submission on the participant, and a packet that silently omits it is worse than one that was never started. The builder contract reaches the same answer mechanically - a component the map names and no artifact renders is requiredComponentsMissing.
rows.aCommittedReleaseBlockerAlreadySaysThis: The track registry carries this as a named release blocker, in its own words: "Master Library Edition 1.1 retains the CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form as a SUPPORTING_PROCESS asset with document role SUPPORTING_FORM, not as a packet form. The authority gate treats a supporting-process asset as one that cannot back an official_pdf_fill component, so every Montana component that maps to it is recorded as an authority role mismatch. ... The mapping is retained rather than dropped ... and the asset-class question is carried here as an explicit release blocker and a proposed Edition 1.2 reclassification. Edition 1.1 is not modified." This lane owns neither the Master Library edition nor the authority gate, so it reports the mismatch rather than editing around it.

whatTheNextLaneStartsWith: The one pinned source binds byte-exact and is held; nothing needs acquiring for it.

Three of the five components are custom_pleading (motion, certificate of service, proposed order) and the fifth is process_guidance. All four are composable today from committed records, on the shared composed-pleading host this lane already reuses.

The legal inputs are settled and unusually complete: fifteen generationRequirements with the participant question for each, four participantFilingRequirements, seven manualCompletionItems, seven selfHelpStopConditions, the venue, the exact DOJ CRISS mailing address and phone and email, and the express rules that no motion fee is identified and that notarization is replaced by a declaration under penalty of perjury.

The build turns on ONE decision that is not this lane's: whether component 4 may be satisfied by the held 2024 DOCX (which needs a governed PDF rendering of the pinned bytes, or an Edition 1.2 reclassification), or whether the component is restated as a participant-obtained document. Either answer unblocks the family; guessing between them does not.

Two participant-facing constraints must survive into any build: the packet must say "sealed and treated as confidential criminal justice information" and never "destroyed" or "erased"; and it must not reproduce DS-100 or DS-200, which carry a non-commercial-use restriction.

The custody reconciliation table data/rcap-grade-a/route-obligation-census-v1/source-custody-reconciliation.json carries no row at all for worklistGroupId mt_deferred_dismissal-set, so family_sources_bind fell through to the census/form-number tier. It bound correctly, but the family has no custody-class determination of its own.
rows.theDeeperFinding: The DOCX is not merely unfillable, it is the WRONG STAGE. The Montana DOJ/DCI Expungement/Removal Request Form is an agency submission a person MAILS AFTER a court has already ordered relief - it lists the court order among its own enclosures, and the committed unit description places it at "The Department of Justice stage, a separate participant submission to a different destination that Sec. 46-18-204(2) places on the participant", after the dismissal order. So the one source this family binds is downstream of the filing the route exists to make. The three components that ARE the court filing - the motion, the certificate of service and the proposed order - bind no source at all: legal-design-specifications.json records all three with templateStatus "not_drafted", and no Montana court instrument for this route exists in any mounted custody. Building around the agency form and calling the result a deferred-dismissal packet would ship a post-order mailing as though it were the motion; drafting the missing motion from the statute would be synthesising the instrument the record does not hold.
rows.independentlyConfirmedBy: The Captain's source-identity sweep reached the same conclusion from the other direction after this row was written, and adds the contrast case: the sibling family mt_misdemeanor_expungement-set DOES hold its court instrument, srmisexp2025.pdf, 22 pages, no AcroForm, carrying the Petition, the Order and the Statement of Inability. That is the Montana pattern - the court instruments exist as flat PDFs where they exist at all - and it is exactly what this family is missing.

rows.appearanceLevelInspection: The delivered PDFs were read back and diffed item by item against the five pinned source documents, rather than trusting the finalizer's report. Both fixtures carry EXACTLY 21 added text items and nothing else across 25 pages: EXP102 page 1 the defendant caption; page 2 first, middle, last, date of birth, street address and city/state/zip; page 6 printed name, address, city/state/zip, phone and email; EXP104 page 1 the defendant caption and nothing anywhere else on that form; EXP105 page 1 the defendant caption and the date of birth and nothing on any of its four pages of findings and orders; EXP101 nothing at all on any of its seven pages; FEE102 page 1 the defendant caption and page 6 name, address, city/state/zip, phone and email. No ink on any signature line, any date line, any certificate of mailing, any qualification box or any judicial finding. Every value sits at rule-y plus two points, inside its measured box.
rows.whatThePacketRefusesToDecide: EXP102 item 9 lists eleven qualification options and this build ticks none. Three are declared NOT_APPLICABLE_ON_THIS_ROUTE against a named route condition, each of them directing the reader on its own printed face to a different court form - EXP106 for subdivisions 1 or 2, EXP107 for the court's inherent authority. The other eight ARE subdivision 3, which is the whole of this route, and which one applies is decided by the disposition and the discharge date rather than by the route. Each of the eight is declared required-before-filing with determinedByTheCaseNotTheRoute and the reason the route cannot settle it, and each is printed in participant-instructions.md with the form's own words and the waiting period the committed registry records. 60 required-before-filing items in total are disclosed; requiredFactsNotCollected is 0 because every one of them is named in the guide.

THE SHARED BUILD HOST SORTED THE PARTICIPANT'S DISCLOSURE LIST ALPHABETICALLY BY FIELD ID. That is the exact defect the composed-pleading host's own comment warns about. Here it printed a sixty-item table with item 16 above item 10, item 2 below both, and item 9's eight qualification options in the order d, h, i, j, f, g, e, c - a table a participant reads top to bottom while working through a petition numbered 1 to 16. rows.whyTheRowGatePassedAnyway: The row gate reports "1/1 source(s) bind" and the family declares TWO. familySources() in scripts/verify-packet-build-environment.mjs builds its source list from the custody reconciliation with `.filter((s) => s.resolved && s.heldAs?.sha256)`, so an UNRESOLVED source is dropped from the list rather than counted as unresolvable. The custody row itself is explicit - data/rcap-grade-a/route-obligation-census-v1/source-custody-reconciliation.json records official-form:ACIC-ORDER-VETERANS-COURT with resolved false and heldAs null, and the row's custodyClass is SOURCE_IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED - so nothing is hidden, but the gate's own denominator is the resolved subset and a lane that read only its summary line would build on one source and never notice the second. Reported, not edited: that script is not an owned path of this lane.
rows.whyTheQueueSaysSourceReadyAnyway: MASTER_QUEUE.json records this family SOURCE_READY with sourceBound true and boundCount 2, resolving the order "committed_acquisition_return_and_governed_custody" against data/rcap-grade-a/packet-factory-24h/disc03/CODEX_CS2_SRC2_ACQUISITION.json, and CAPTAIN_SOURCE_IDENTITY_DETERMINATIONS.json gives the next action as "Build from the already-bound petition and newly custodied veterans-court order." The acquisition return it points at does not support that. Its own entry for this item records result ACQUIRED_CURRENT_OFFICIAL_BINARY with a privateArtifactReceipt whose provider is Google Drive, shared false and visibility owner_only, and beside it an uploadFailure: "GitHub workflow dispatch returned HTTP 403; the uploader also rejects media.ark.org because it cannot encode the verified ACIC-page-to-CDN provenance chain." A Google Drive file id is not a custody. The corpus index says the same thing about the fourteen src05 binaries in its own custody note: bytesHeldByAnyMountedCustody false, "the bytes were never staged, committed, or added to any release, and no mounted custody holds them".
rows.theBytesAreRecoverableAndThatIsTheUseful: The Drive object still exists and still matches. Read at 2026-09-09: file id 1fd3o7fV3S0BUug-aPRPd4NmPbe0_LDvX, title CODEX-CS2-SRC2__AR-VETERANS-COURT-SET__ACIC-ORDER-VETERANS-COURT__dd73dfdee29c.pdf, mimeType application/pdf, fileSize 116034 - byte-for-byte the byteLength the acquisition return recorded - owner roger@legalease.com. Metadata only was read; the file was NOT downloaded, not staged and not committed. So this is a custody and indexing gap rather than a lost source, and it is one owner action from closed.
exactRemedy: Stage the Drive object into a declared custody, verify it hashes to dd73dfdee29c12977a360413311a973fd3366e5a7dc606d385666bfa3b38ccf5, and add an entry for it to data/rcap-all50/local-source-corpus-index.json under that custody.

Then the family builds on the path this lane has already proved out: both ACIC forms are flat PDFs with acroFieldCount 0, which is exactly the measured-flat-overlay shape used for mn_petition_609a02_subd3-set in this same return.
rows.whyNotBuiltFromThePetitionAlone: The committed packet set for ar-veterans-court-set has three components and ALL THREE are requirement "required": process guidance, the ACIC petition, and the ACIC order (ar-veterans-court-proposed-order-3, outputStrategy official_pdf_fill, officialFormId ACIC-ORDER-VETERANS-COURT). The two routeKeys are a two-stage route and stage 2 is recorded as "Stage 2 files the ACIC veterans treatment court petition and order pair" - the pair, not the petition. Shipping the petition without the order would hand a participant a filing that asks a court to sign an order the packet does not contain, and would read as built. The builder contract reaches the same answer mechanically: a component the map names and no artifact renders is requiredComponentsMissing.
rows.whyNotSubstituted: The obvious substitute is the ACIC order held for a sibling Arkansas family. It is a different form for a different statutory route, and CAPTAIN_SOURCE_IDENTITY_DETERMINATIONS.json states the governing rule in its own words: a determination "never satisfies one identity by binding the binary of another". No order from another route was considered further.
foundAndNotFixed: family_sources_bind in scripts/verify-packet-build-environment.mjs reports its ratio over the RESOLVED subset of a family's sources rather than over the sources the family declares, because familySources() filters unresolved entries out of the list instead of adding them to `unresolvable`. On this family that prints "1/1 source(s) bind by exact SHA-256" for a family whose custody row records one of its two sources unresolved. The check is not wrong about the source it examined; its denominator hides the one it dropped.
